evidence.snippet: - A builder starts when its pull request is in the merge queue, not when it merges. If the queue then ejects that pull request, the builder comments `Released:` on the issue it took next and goes back to the ejected pull request. Another builder can then take the released issue, starting from any branch the first one pushed. A builder never holds a claim it isn't working on.

- Use as many branches as the work needs. A builder pushes each pull request to a branch of its own, named for its issue, such as `claude/issue-<n>-<words>`, and asks nobody before creating one: the maintainer said on 2026-11-20, in the coordinator's session, "they can use as many branches as they need", after builders in cloud sessions kept stopping to ask him for a second branch. That covers a builder's own branches for issues it has claimed. It never pushes to another builder's branch, to `main`, or to `melian/state`, and never forces a push.

- One issue is one pull request. A step that needs several is split into an issue per pull request, each blocked by the one before. Open the draft with `Closes #<n>` in its description; a fix pass for a review finding works on the same issue and pull request.

verification.reason: The base decision says only that a second builder takes a released issue "starting from any branch the first one pushed". It does not say the second builder pushes to that branch. The head rule, "never pushes to another builder's branch", lets B base its own `claude/issue-600-…` branch on A's pushed work. It also explicitly lets B create branches for issues it has claimed without asking anyone, so the handoff still works. The claim needs a stronger reading, that "starting from" means pushing onto A's branch and keeping A's draft. Neither decision says that. "One issue is one pull request" is about splitting a step into one issue per pull request. It doesn't say a released issue's draft can't be replaced. Because the cited words forbid nothing the new line does, there is no traced contradiction. The scenario shows an unstated edge case, namely what happens to A's orphaned draft. That is a documentation gap, not a conflict with an ACTIVE decision.
